Lelow Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lelów, Poland

Demolished. Jews are recorded in Lelów from the 16th century; in the second half of the 18th century, Tzadik Dawid Biedermann - student of Elimelech of Leżajsk - settled there and founded the Lelów Hasidic dynasty, growing the community to 60% (720) of the population by 1897. About 700 Jews were deported to Treblinka in September 1942; the tzadik's descendants now live in Israel. This cemetery, established by the 17th century, once housed a wooden ohel over Biedermann's grave (d. January 28, 1814) - destroyed in WWII, with the site later built over by a Communist-era trading pavilion. In 1988, Abraham Biderman and the Nissenbaum Family Foundation confirmed the tzadik's remains lay beneath the pavilion itself, prompting a symbolic ohel inside a partitioned room. Legal ownership was resolved by 2009, transferring the plot to the Leżajsk-Poland Hasid Foundation; a new dedicated ohel was constructed 2012-2014 after partial pavilion demolition, and the grave has since become an international Hasidic pilgrimage site.
